summary: The deterministic verdict is PASS (analysis-result.json#/policy_verdict), with run_validity VALID and analysis_coverage COMPLETE (no reasons). The only evaluated policy, overall-errors, compares observed error_rate_ratio 0/2623 against threshold 0.01 with operator lte and reports status PASS. All six transactions (add product to cart, cart, checkout, home, product, reset cart) also report error_count 0. Latency percentiles are low overall (p50 11ms, p95 46ms, p99 77ms); home has the highest transaction percentiles (p50 27ms, p95 61ms, p99 96ms), and the overall max of 904ms is a single-sample outlier far above the p99. throughput_rps is stored as numerator/denominator pairs whose semantics are not defined in the evidence. No findings were generated. Advisory notes are limits only: zero recorded errors do not prove error absence, the single 904ms max warrants a bounded check, no temporal data supports causal or lead/lag claims, and advice does not alter the PASS verdict.

hypotheses.observation: Overall latency shows max 904ms while p50 is 11ms, p95 46ms, and p99 77ms; home is the highest transaction at max 904ms, p50 27ms, p95 61ms, p99 96ms.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The 904ms value is a single-sample maximum that is far above the p99; it could reflect a cold start, JIT/GC pause, resource contention, or one slow request, but the stored evidence contains no per-sample timeline to confirm which.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Inspect the individual sample records around the 904ms maximum (index, timestamps, response size, thread state) and correlate with GC/thread/network logs for the run window before treating it as a systemic latency event.

hypotheses.observation: error_count is 0 and error_rate_ratio is 0/2623 overall, and 0/437 or 0/438 for every transaction; the policy check on the overall ratio passes with status PASS.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: Either the tested environment truly served every request, or errors were not captured because sampler/assertion configuration did not register them (e.g., unasserted HTTP status codes, non-HTTP failures, or a sampler that only records a subset of outcomes).
hypotheses.recommended_check: Verify the JMeter assertion and response-code handling for each sampler so that 4xx/5xx, timeouts, and connection failures would increment error_count; re-run a deliberate failure probe to confirm error detection works.

hypotheses.observation: Transaction sample counts are nearly equal across scopes: add product to cart 437, cart 437, checkout 437, home 438, product 437, reset cart 437, summing to the overall 2623.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The workload appears to be a scripted loop with equal iterations per transaction rather than a realistic traffic mix; this balanced pattern constrains what the metrics can say about production-shaped load.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Review the JMeter thread group, loop, pacing, and ramp configuration and compare the executed mix with the intended workload model before extrapolating to other traffic distributions.

hypotheses.observation: throughput_rps is stored as numerator/denominator pairs, e.g., overall 2623000/44986 and per-transaction 437000/44986; no definition of these fields appears in the evidence.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: If read as quotient requests-per-second these fields would imply a modest throughput (~58 rps overall and ~10 rps per transaction), but the semantics of numerator and denominator are not stated, so the actual throughput and whether it matched the intended load profile are unknown.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Confirm the definition of throughput_rps numerator and denominator against the collector implementation, then compare reported values with the target load profile and ramp schedule for the run.

recommendations.action: Preserve and report the deterministic verdict PASS unchanged from the policy check (observed error_rate_ratio 0/2623, threshold 0.01, operator lte).
recommendations.rationale: The referenced policy check has status PASS and run validity VALID; advisory interpretation must not modify that verdict.

recommendations.action: Before citing the 904ms maximum, examine the surrounding sample records and runtime logs to determine whether it is a one-off cold-start/contention event or a repeated pattern.
recommendations.rationale: The max is a single-sample value far above the overall p99 (77ms) and home p99 (96ms), so it should not be generalized without a bounded check.

recommendations.action: Validate the error-detection configuration so that error_count 0 can be trusted as an absence of recorded errors rather than a recording gap.
recommendations.rationale: All scopes report 0 errors, but this only means what the samplers/assertions captured; unasserted status codes or non-HTTP failures would be invisible to the policy check.

recommendations.action: Confirm the throughput_rps numerator/denominator semantics and compare the executed load with the intended target before making any capacity or headroom statements.
recommendations.rationale: The evidence stores throughput as unexplained numerator/denominator pairs; a quotient interpretation (e.g., ~58 rps overall) is not confirmed by the evidence and the run may have been under- or over-loaded relative to intent.

recommendations.action: If latency behavior matters beyond error rate, add latency-based policies (e.g., p95/p99 SLO checks) on the same evidence so they can be evaluated in future runs.
recommendations.rationale: Only the overall error rate policy was evaluated in this analysis; latency percentiles were recorded but no latency policy result exists in the evidence.

caveats: The deterministic verdict is PASS with run_validity VALID and analysis_coverage COMPLETE; this advice does not and cannot change that outcome.

The evidence contains no timestamps, epoch deltas, or clock relationship, so no lead/lag ordering, trend analysis, or temporal causal hypothesis is supported; verify clock/collection timing before any such inference.

error_count 0 and error_rate_ratio 0/2623 cover only this run's 2623 samples; they do not prove absence of errors in production, under other loads, or under different assertion/error-capture settings.
The findings array is empty and no anomalies are reported; absence of findings does not prove stability, spare capacity, or low risk under conditions not exercised by this run.
The 904ms overall max is a single-sample value; percentiles (overall p99 77ms) indicate most samples are far lower, so the max alone should not be used as a typical latency claim.

throughput_rps numerator/denominator semantics are not defined in the referenced fields; any quotient interpretation (e.g., ~58 rps overall) is unconfirmed and should be validated against the collector definition.
Only the overall error rate policy (overall-errors) was checked; latency thresholds and per-transaction policies were not evaluated, and a missing policy check is not equivalent to a pass.
There is no baseline or comparative environment evidence, so no attribution of delays, errors, or most-likely causes to any event is supported.
